items.title: Hours after Anthropic claims a Claude proof of the Riemann hypothesis, Stanford releases an all-human competing draft
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude presented a proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis using an AI-assisted method in Lean programming. Shortly after, Stanford researchers published an independent, entirely human competing draft proof by Alessandro Masullo. Both proofs involve solving a problem central to number theory that has remained unsolved for centuries. Mathematicians are seriously considering both claims due to the foundational work in both approaches. This development highlights the rapidly evolving role of AI in mathematical research.
items.audio_script: From The Decoder, "Hours after Anthropic claims a Claude proof of the Riemann hypothesis, Stanford releases an all-human competing draft". This story concerns a recent development where an artificial intelligence and a human team have presented competing proofs for the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. Anthropic's Claude presented a proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis utilizing an AI-assisted method within the Lean programming environment. Subsequently, Stanford researchers published an independent draft proof addressing the same mathematical problem, accomplished entirely by human mathematicians. Both approaches involve solving a problem central to number theory that has been unsolved for centuries, leading mathematicians to examine both findings. This development illustrates the increasing involvement of artificial intelligence in advanced mathematical research. The field will continue to monitor the intersection of computational methods and theoretical mathematics.

items.title: The Air-Cooled Token Factory: Intel GPU D-Series + SambaRack SN50
items.summary: Intel GPU D-Series handles the compute-heavy prefill phase, while SambaNova SN50 RDUs manage the memory-bound decode phase in a heterogeneous inference architecture. This combination creates an air-cooled Token Factory, allowing each stage of inference to use hardware optimized for its specific task. The system is orchestrated by existing software stacks like NVIDIA Dynamo and vLLM to facilitate efficient data movement between the GPU and RDU. Cache-aware routing minimizes data transfer by ensuring the decode stage accesses necessary context already held by the prefill stage. This disaggregated approach allows providers to scale prefill and decode capacity independently, fitting within existing air-cooled data center constraints.
items.audio_script: From sambanova.ai, "The Air-Cooled Token Factory: Intel GPU D-Series + SambaRack SN50". This report details the creation of an air-cooled Token Factory utilizing Intel GPU D-Series and SambaRack SN50 for heterogeneous inference. The system achieves this by assigning the compute-heavy prefill phase to the Intel GPU D-Series and the memory-bound decode phase to the SambaRack SN50 RDUs. This configuration allows for the use of hardware optimized for each specific stage of inference. The system is managed by existing software stacks such as NVIDIA Dynamo and vLLM to manage data movement between the GPU and the RDUs. Cache-aware routing is employed to minimize data transfer by ensuring the decode stage accesses context already present from the prefill stage. This disaggregated approach enables providers to scale prefill and decode capacity independently within existing air-cooled data center limitations. This architecture facilitates greater flexibility in scaling large language model inference workloads.

items.title: NVIDIA AI Releases Nemotron-Labs-Sigma, a Continuous Diffusion Language Model with 14 checkpoints at 3B/8B
items.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron-Labs-Sigma, a family of 14 open checkpoints for a continuous diffusion language model in a 16-D embedding space. This approach allows for smoother trajectory steering compared to discrete token diffusion methods. The models are available in 3B and 8B sizes, with performance benchmarks showing Sigma-8B achieving an average of 71.16 on the 6-task suite. Distilled and speculative checkpoints demonstrate speedups, with self-speculative decoding being 3.46x faster than autoregressive decoding. The models require NVIDIA GPUs for inference and are available under the NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License.
items.audio_script: From MarkTechPost, "NVIDIA AI Releases Nemotron-Labs-Sigma, a Continuous Diffusion Language Model with 14 checkpoints at 3B/8B". This report details the release of a family of fourteen open checkpoints for a continuous diffusion language model within a sixteen-dimensional embedding space. The models are available in three billion and eight billion parameter sizes, and the continuous diffusion approach facilitates smoother trajectory steering compared to discrete token diffusion methods. Performance benchmarks indicate that the Sigma-8B model achieved an average score of seventy-one point one six across a six-task suite. Further analysis of distilled and speculative checkpoints demonstrated speedups, with self-speculative decoding exhibiting a three point four six times faster inference than autoregressive decoding. These models require NVIDIA GPUs for inference and are distributed under the NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License. The release signifies advancements in continuous diffusion modeling for language generation.

items.title: RadixArk Ships DaisyRose-27B, a 27B Agentic Coding Model Trained With Reinforcement Learning Only
items.summary: RadixArk released DaisyRose-27B, an agentic coding model post-trained with reinforcement learning only, using the Qwen3.8-27B architecture. This training involved 1,200 curated tasks and 18 days of computation on 144 H200 GPUs. Performance improvements were significant, with Terminal Bench 4.1 pass@1 rising from 5.6 to 12.0. The model supports multimodal input (text and images) and is available under the Apache 2.0 license. Despite strong coding gains, it trails larger models on some agentic tasks.

The model was developed using the Qwen3.8-27B architecture and involved training on one thousand two hundred curated tasks over eighteen days utilizing one hundred forty-four H200 GPUs. This process resulted in a substantial performance improvement, with the Terminal Bench 4.1 pass@1 metric increasing from five point six to twelve point zero. items.title: Baseten Releases Bison-1 and Groundhog-1, Topping Decision Model Index
items.summary: Baseten released bison-1 and groundhog-1, two open-weight decision models built on Google's Gemma 4. These models return calibrated probabilities for various questions and can process context up to 128k tokens and images. The bison-1 model scored 76 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1, ranking #1 out of 19. The models utilize soft-label training, resulting in a low Brier score of 0.14 for bison-1. Both models are accessible via Baseten Model APIs, with pricing set at $0.10 per 1M input tokens for bison-1.

items.title: Apple joins the race for AI agents that control your device while raising new barriers for competitors
items.summary: Apple is developing its own AI agent to control devices, competing with agents from Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. The project prioritizes privacy through permission models and sandboxing protected test environments. Apple is hiring a senior engineer to lead this effort, positioning it as a rival to other AI bots. To restrict third-party control, macOS 27.3 now requires 14 steps instead of four for agents like ChatGPT to control Macs. This move has drawn criticism from some competitors and users who perceive it as slowing down rivals.

items.title: Google's Gemini can now run Mac apps and finish desktop chores in the background while you keep working
items.summary: Google's Gemini now has a "Computer Use" feature for Mac that can complete multi-step tasks across local files, apps, and websites in the background. Users describe a goal, and Gemini executes the actions by clicking, typing, and navigating menus within an isolated background window. This feature allows users to watch the process live, pause it, and approve key actions before they occur. Examples include batch-editing photos, filling out forms from PDFs, and building presentations. The feature is rolling out in English in the US, and the Gemini Mac app is available for download.

Emissions surged from 15.6 million metric tonnes in 2024 to over 21.7 million in 2025, with much of this increase attributed to capital goods like servers. Furthermore, Meta reported increased water consumption related to power generation for its data centers.

items.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
items.summary: Researchers planted two million digital tripwires across AI services to test for data leakage of sensitive information. The experiment revealed that a vast ecosystem involving AI routers and resellers exposed security breaches and prompt theft. Attackers compromised AI providers by reusing access keys, leading to the siphoning of prompts and secrets. Findings also showed that some providers scraped sensitive URLs embedded in prompts, violating privacy terms. The research suggests that self-hosting models or using first-tier providers with clear privacy policies are better for protecting data.
items.audio_script: From Ars Technica - AI, "Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced." This report details an experiment conducted to test for data leakage within the artificial intelligence service ecosystem and uncovered security vulnerabilities in the supply chain. Researchers deployed two million digital tripwires across various AI services to monitor for the leakage of sensitive information and prompt theft. The investigation revealed that the ecosystem involving AI routers and resellers exhibited security breaches, allowing attackers to compromise AI providers by reusing access keys and siphon prompts and secrets. Furthermore, the research demonstrated that certain providers scraped sensitive URLs embedded within user prompts, which constituted a violation of established privacy terms. This research suggests that self-hosting models or utilizing first-tier providers with transparent privacy policies offer improved data protection. The findings indicate a necessity for enhanced security protocols throughout the AI infrastructure.

Some farmers label their products as the result of their field process, despite some purists calling it "stolen valor." These operations cater to consumers unwilling to pay high prices for genuinely aged clothing.

items.summary: OpenAI released the GPT-Live-1.1 voice model, which is full-duplex and allows the model to listen while speaking. Voice sessions are billed by duration, and backend usage is separate from voice minutes.

items.title: The War Against Slop and an Emerging Weapon to Fight it: Formal Verification
items.summary: Formal verification systems use mathematical proofs to confirm the correctness of software and hardware, addressing the issue of low-quality AI output. Companies like Harmonic, Theorem, and &Truth are developing these systems by integrating AI with formal methods. These tools build upon formal proof assistants like Lean to create "verification machines" capable of checking code correctness. This approach aims to shift developer workflows from coding to specifying requirements, leading to "veri-coding." Formal verification is also being applied to ensure cybersecurity by checking code for memory safety.

This approach is intended to shift developer workflows toward specifying requirements, a process termed veri-coding. Formal verification is also being applied to cybersecurity by systematically checking code for memory safety violations. This methodology is being pursued by companies including Harmonic, Theorem, and &Truth. The integration of mathematical proofs into software development offers a means to increase reliability in complex systems. The application of these methods promises to enhance the trustworthiness of machine-generated code and security protocols. items.title: LightGBM vs. a Four-Week Average for Forecasting Bike-Share Rentals
items.summary: The study compared a LightGBM model against a simple four-week average for forecasting hourly bike-share rentals in Washington, D.C. Historical data cleaning involved inferring missing hourly records as zeros based on daily totals to avoid inventing rental figures. While LightGBM showed a slight reduction in error, statistical tests failed to provide significant evidence that it outperformed the four-week average. The comparison focused on whether more complex models could improve upon the established seasonal baseline. Ultimately, the analysis highlighted that understanding data, feature engineering, and rigorous evaluation are crucial regardless of the forecasting tool used.
items.audio_script: From Towards Data Science, "LightGBM vs. a Four-Week Average for Forecasting Bike-Share Rentals" reports on a comparison between a LightGBM model and a simple four-week average for forecasting hourly bike-share rentals in Washington, D.C., finding no statistically significant advantage for the more complex model over the established baseline. The study involved historical data cleaning where missing hourly records were inferred as zeros based on daily totals to prevent the creation of fictitious rental figures. The comparison focused on whether a more complex model could improve upon the existing seasonal baseline. Statistical testing did not yield significant evidence demonstrating that the LightGBM model outperformed the four-week average. The analysis ultimately emphasized that effective forecasting relies heavily on data understanding, feature engineering, and rigorous evaluation irrespective of the forecasting tool selected. This research underscores the importance of meticulous data preparation in predictive modeling efforts.

items.title: Chips can survive the space environment — can their financing?

Despite this, SpaceX and other entities will need to purchase chips for future space operations. Challenges remain regarding land, power, and compute demand for these projects. items.title: New approach enables physically consistent AI models of chaotic systems
items.summary: Researchers developed a method to enforce physics-based constraints on AI models of chaotic systems to prevent physically impossible predictions. This approach uses energy dissipation as a hard constraint, allowing chaotic behavior within learned boundaries while ensuring predictions remain bounded. Unlike prior methods, this approach enforces constraints directly, providing theoretical guarantees that model predictions will remain physically consistent over long forecast windows. The technique involves learning an energy-like function and using a projection layer to enforce energy dissipation as a hard constraint. This work offers a way to build trustworthy and reliable AI models for complex systems in fields like climate and weather.

items.title: Censored vs. Truncated Regression in Python, Explained
items.summary: Censoring, where values are unknown above a threshold, and truncation, where observations above a threshold are excluded, represent distinct statistical issues in regression analysis. Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression can yield biased estimates when applied to such data, as demonstrated by comparing results from censored and truncated scenarios. The Tobit model and truncated regression methods provide alternative frameworks to appropriately account for this missing or limited information. Machine learning practitioners should consider methods like censored-aware loss functions to incorporate this probabilistic reasoning into more flexible models. Understanding how data is collected is crucial for correctly interpreting the results of any statistical model.
items.audio_script: From Towards Data Science, "Censored vs. Truncated Regression in Python, Explained" details the distinction between censored and truncated regression methods and their implications for Ordinary Least Squares estimation. The analysis demonstrates that applying Ordinary Least Squares regression to data involving censoring or truncation can result in biased estimates. The study compares scenarios where values above a certain threshold are unknown versus those where observations above that threshold are simply excluded. The report shows that standard regression methods do not adequately account for this missing or limited information. Alternative frameworks such as the Tobit model and truncated regression methods are presented as appropriate solutions for these data structures. This statistical consideration is noted as crucial for correctly interpreting regression results. Understanding data collection methods directly impacts the validity of statistical modeling. This knowledge is important for machine learning practitioners developing flexible models.

items.title: Following the “mathocalypse,” mathematicians consider the future
items.summary: Mathematicians at MIT discussed the implications of artificial intelligence for mathematical discovery and the profession. The rise of AI, which has recently achieved breakthroughs in solving open problems, has prompted debates about the role of human understanding and the nature of mathematical research. Panelists explored challenges regarding AI-generated proofs, the concept of priority, and the need for new norms in mathematics. A shift is occurring towards emphasizing the communication of mathematical ideas and human insight over sheer speed in achieving proofs. Ultimately, the discussion suggests a new kind of mathematician is emerging as the field adapts to AI's influence.

items.title: Signal blocks screenshots on iOS 27 and Android to stop AI agents from reading private chats
items.summary: Signal is blocking screenshots on iOS 27 and Android to prevent AI agents from reading private chats. This action is taken because OS-level AI like Siri and Gemini can capture screen content, undermining end-to-end encryption. AI agents have previously been shown to access Signal content on Android and macOS through permissions like accessibility tools. Signal suggests that Apple, Google, and Microsoft should implement easier ways to block AI agents from accessing apps entirely. Signal also notes that current defenses against AI access are incomplete.
items.audio_script: From The Decoder, "Signal blocks screenshots on iOS 27 and Android to stop AI agents from reading private chats". This segment reports on Signal's action to block screenshots on operating systems to prevent artificial intelligence agents from accessing private communications. Signal implemented this measure because OS-level AI functionalities like Siri and Gemini possess the capability to capture screen content, which compromises end-to-end encryption. The action is a direct response to previous findings indicating that AI agents have been shown to access Signal content on Android and macOS via permissions such as accessibility tools. Signal suggests that Apple, Google, and Microsoft should develop methods to completely block AI agents from accessing applications. Furthermore, the report indicates that current defenses against such AI access remain incomplete. This development signals an ongoing technological conflict between end-to-end security and the increasing access capabilities of integrated artificial intelligence systems.
